name: Acronym & Abbreviation Profiling
description: Analyzes patterns of acronym definition, frequency, and contextual appropriateness
mechanism: This method evaluates how a text introduces and utilizes acronyms and abbreviations. Human domain experts typically use industry-specific acronyms seamlessly, assuming a baseline level of reader knowledge. In contrast, LLMs—trained on broad corpora with safety and clarity RLHF guardrails—often over-explain acronyms. They compulsively define well-known acronyms (e.g., 'NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)') and maintain an artificially rigid 'define-on-first-use' policy even in informal or highly specialized contexts. By identifying the ratio of defined vs. undefined acronyms and tracing their frequency, the system calculates an 'over-explanation penalty'.
parameters:
Analysis type: Heuristic syntax mapping
Media: Text
Input: Formatted markup/text
Required: Min 100 words with >1 potential capitalized abbreviation
Output: Naturalness score (0-100)
Processing: Rule-based heuristic tree
accuracy: Moderate — 65-80%. Highly dependent on the perceived formality of the prompt topic. Excellent at detecting AI 'mansplaining'.
source: Pragmatic linguistics and LLM alignment safety research.
useCase: Detecting text generated by overly-aligned LLMs that prioritize absolute clarity over human-like contextual shorthand.
strengths:
• Targets core RLHF alignment traits rather than just next-token distributions
• Fast heuristic mapping without heavy NLP embeddings
• Effective at catching 'helper-bot' writing styles
limitations:
• Susceptible to human writers who rigidly adhere to strict style guides (like APA format)
• Ineffective on texts that naturally avoid acronyms
• Works best as a secondary or confirming signal

references.title: Ouyang, L., et al. (2022). Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback. NeurIPS.
